blockedBy: RSFA-DECISION-1: which address is the 'property' on boarder declarations
review.meaning: names, household numbers, boarder names, amounts and frequencies confirmed against the printed form and the live labels; the property address source is a material business decision.
openQuestions: RSFA-DECISION-1: which address is the 'property' on boarder declarations: legacy = applicant 1 physical address, printed as Street / Province / Country (Suburb and City never printed); proposal ASB-ADDR-1..4 = 1st Property Address Street / Suburb / City / Postcode (preview PDF provided). Either way the parts come from Make's OpenAI address split (module 26), which is not deterministic.
RSFA-DECISION-2: pre-fill the customer's signature dates with today: legacy pre-fills both signature dates with today (DDMMYYYY, format inferred from the 8-cell comb); proposal = leave them blank.
The template is owner-encrypted by ASB and filled with an incremental save keeping ASB's encryption (D-007).

corrections.decisionRef: RSFA-DECISION-1: which address is the 'property' on boarder declarations
corrections.reason: Proposed: print the security/purchase property (as BNZ Boarder) as Street / Suburb / City. The legacy lines are Street / Province / Country, so Suburb and City are never printed.
corrections.evidence: The declaration describes the property where the boarders live (ASB: 'your main owner-occupied residence'). The legacy rule uses the applicant's physical address (OpenAI-split parts of text_mkzvrrfx); BNZ Boarder (tested, deployed) uses 1st Property Address (text_mkzvqaw7, split into Street/Suburb/City/Postcode by Make module 26). Both are in the Make contract. Which one is right depends on the deal (purchase vs refinance).
